name: Hutchinson Utilities Commission Pipeline
researcher_notes: Not an existing row: no Hutchinson, Trimont or New Ulm entry in the roster context. Hutchinson Utilities Commission is an intrastate municipal utility, so FERC silence is expected. An April 2003 Industrial Info Resources article gives 89 miles, 16 inch from Trimont to New Ulm (34 miles), 12 inch from New Ulm to Hutchinson, and 60,000 MMBtu per day. A 2003 Minnesota Court of Appeals decision on the certificate of need and a Minnesota Public Utilities Commission order cover the 89 mile line and about $26 million cost. The City of New Ulm utilities page says gas reaches New Ulm from Northern Border at Trimont over the Hutchinson pipeline, so the line is operating. Capacity 60,000 MMBtu per day is only in the 2003 article and is left unfilled because the unit is not a sheet unit and the figure is a design number. Construction year 2003 comes from the pre-construction article; exact in-service date not found. The diameter is 16 in then 12 in, entered as 16;12 (confirm the sheet multi-value format). Length 89 mi is over the 25 km add threshold. Route not researched; no official GIS found. Owner name matches the ownership team spelling exactly. Confidence medium: the sources are 2003 and a current municipal page, and the justia fetch was read through a search summary because the page hit a bot wall.
